indication: [AGE]-year-old [GENDER], status post craniotomy for brain tumor 9 days ago. Presents with worsening dyspnea. Chest X-ray was negative for pneumonia or CHF. Evaluate for pulmonary embolism or malignancy.
technique: ** Helical CT acquisition was performed from the lung apices through the diaphragm following the administration of intravenous contrast bolus timed for optimal opacification of the pulmonary arteries. Multiplanar reformats were reviewed.
findings:
**
The lungs are clear without evidence of focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. There is no suspicious pulmonary nodule or mass identified to suggest primary lung malignancy. The tracheobronchial tree is patent throughout.
Regarding the pulmonary vasculature, there are large filling defects noted within the main pulmonary artery bilaterally. These extend into both the right and left main pulmonary arteries and involve the proximal lobar branches centrally. The distal segmental and subsegmental arteries appear patent. There is mild enlargement of the main pulmonary artery trunk, though the right ventricle remains normal in size relative to the left ventricle, and there is no evidence of right ventricular strain.
The heart is normal in size. The pericardium is thin and unremarkable. The thoracic aorta and its primary branches demonstrate normal caliber and course.
Within the mediastinum, there is no lymphadenopathy. The esophagus is midline and unremarkable. Minor degenerative changes are noted in the thoracic spine, specifically some mild marginal osteophyte formation at the T7-T8 levels. A small, benign-appearing simple cyst is noted in the lower lobe of the liver visualized on the inferior cuts. The visualized portions of the adrenal glands are normal.
conclusion:
**
Bilateral central pulmonary emboli involving the main and proximal lobar pulmonary arteries. No evidence of right ventricular strain.
